text: This humanoid waters three simulated plants. Its articulated body and the ballistic water parcels run on the NVIDIA GPU.
Both sides use the same body controller and disturbances. Each pot should receive sixty millilitres. Completion receipts are lost.
On the left, a timeout creates a new command identifier. The executor treats the retry as another watering job, even after the first pour succeeded.
On the right, retries keep one identifier. Fresh observations confirm water arriving in the pot, so the coordinator can move to the next plant without a receipt.
The blue parcels follow gravity from the measured nozzle pose. Water counts only when a parcel crosses a pot's capture region. The plots report measured delivery, not the intended target.
The stable identifier alone blocks duplicate pours, but does not complete the remaining plants when receipts never arrive. Observation-based completion supplies that missing step.

There is a cost. Here receipts work, but observations stop. This queue-aware policy holds after the first plant, while the receipt-driven controller continues. More awareness is not automatically better.
This is one synthetic configuration, not a reliability claim. The wrist tool is fixed, the water is ballistic, and neither soil physics nor hardware operation has been validated.
